_source: Detector thresholds. startup_* values are from countinghouse (server/src/rules.ts, derive.ts, advisor.ts). personal_* values are from dime by Charles Zheng, https://github.com/goodnight000/dime (server/cfo.ts, server/money.ts). Dime has no license file in its repository as of 2026-10-09, so only the numbers and formulas are carried, as reimplemented logic, not its code.

startup.duplicate_rule: same normalized vendor and identical amount on a card account within 3 days
startup.unusual_note: Source: a first-ever payment to a vendor of $5,000 or more, or a charge over 4x the vendor's median with at least 4 charges on record and over $2,000. Transfers, Payroll and Payroll Taxes are exempt.
startup.payroll_load_note: Source adds 25% to salary for taxes and benefits when modeling a hire. Default salary in the source scenario was 160000.
startup.contractor_1099_verify: The source uses $600. Check the current IRS threshold for the payment year; a law change may have raised it for payments made after 2025.
startup.runway_fundraise_note: Source tells the founder to start Series A prep when runway falls to 9 months.
startup.spike_note: Chosen here, never measured. The source flags AWS +38% since June by eye; it has no coded spike threshold. The 30 percent borrows dime's category trend threshold.

personal.daily_number: pool = income - bills - invest - discretionary spend this month - sweeps to goals this month; today = max(0, floor(pool at start of day / days left including today) - spent today)
personal.sweep: Leftover from today moves to the active goal at midnight and leaves the pool, so under-spending does not inflate tomorrow. Overspending lowers the pool, so tomorrow shrinks by itself.
personal.girl_math_pace: average sweep over the last 7 days, else a quarter of today's number, never below $1 a day
personal.girl_math_delay_days: ceil(price / pace); under one day of pace say hours
personal.parking_rule: Money for a goal under 2 years out sits in cash; over 2 years, an index fund. (Dime's literacy moment. Education, not advice.)
personal.impulse_rule: 24-hour wait on purchases above today's number (the Reddit-sourced waiting period Dime built a feature around).
